title: Contemporary welfare receipt has heterogeneous and program-specific political participation associations
source_unit: Young U.S. adults in nationally representative longitudinal survey data on welfare receipt and political participation

observations.period: Contemporary welfare receipt and political participation; Social Problems volume 69 issue 3, 2022

denominator.unit: nationally representative longitudinal survey study frame; abstract does not state one pooled respondent denominator

cash_assistance_and_participation.unit: reported fixed-effects association with political participation

food_stamps_and_registration.value: positively associated with being registered to vote

food_stamps_and_voting.value: countervailing associations, including marginalizing and incorporating patterns, depending on political attentiveness

observations.method: Social Problems article using nationally representative data and fixed-effects models adjusting for time-stable unobserved characteristics and observed time-varying factors to study cash assistance, food stamps, registration, voting, and political attentiveness among young adults.
observations.uncertainty: The abstract reports adjusted associations, not a randomized treatment effect. It does not identify a dated benefit episode, administrative receipt, benefit adequacy, caseworker interaction, blame, trust change, or verified turnout for a named individual.
observations.subgroup: Young adults, with heterogeneity by program and political attentiveness.
observations.counterinterpretation: Null cash-assistance associations and mixed food-stamp associations can reflect selection, program design, benefit amount, stigma, administrative experience, political attention, or different resource effects. Registration is not turnout, and participation is not institutional trust.

related_sources.claim: Oxford Academic DOI and publication metadata identify the article and authors Naomi F. Sugie and Emma Conner.
JSTOR landing page identifies the published Social Problems article and issue placement.

boundary: This is a contemporary U.S. welfare-participation association with program and attentiveness heterogeneity, not a universal cash effect, causal benefit-to-vote estimate, or trust/legitimacy result.
